sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: As of the Nov 25 close, the S&P 500 sits at 7,183, about 6.4% below its level a month ago and in the lower third of its 1-month range (high 7,744, low 6,910). The Nasdaq 100 is weaker at 26,047, down 11.0% over the month and near the bottom of its range (high 29,813, low 25,029). The VIX closed at 28.3, up from 18.4 a month ago, and the Euro Stoxx 50 closed at the low of its 1-month range, down 4.2% over five sessions. The week carries 32 scheduled reports from the tracked universe, with technology names making up about half.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon: ORCL US and CRDO US report in technology, and NKE US in consumer-cyclical. Wed: SNOW US and ZS US report into technology, whose median 3-day reaction is -0.1% across 810 names, so there is no strong sector tilt to lean on. Thu is the heaviest day with 14 reports, including MU US (technology), DG US (consumer-defensive, median -0.3%) and ULTA US (consumer-cyclical, median +0.3%). None of the week's names sit in the three sectors with the largest recent reactions. All dates are still estimated, not confirmed.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: The largest recent median reactions are in mining (+4.6% median, 229 tickers, 2,766 news items), copper (-2.5%, 6 tickers, 231 items) and energy (+2.0%, 328 tickers, 5,173 items). Mining and energy have thick news windows; copper is a thin sample of six names. Sectors holding this week's reporters are flat by comparison, with medians between -0.3% and +0.3%.
